C0.quote: each voter has as many votes as there are open seats
C0.note: Compares multi-seat plurality and cumulative voting as election procedures, with theory and a lab experiment on turnout and minority seats.

C1.quote: A lab experiment based on a costly voting design strongly supports both
C1.note: Proposition 1 and the costly-voting equilibria are equilibrium analysis (EQ); the numerical equilibrium computations in Section 3.3 are treated as part of EQ, not as SI. The main results tested and reported are experimental (EM).

C2.1.value: votes; profiles of votes (x_p); ballots not named as such
C2.1.quote: We call xp the profiles of votes cast by members of party

C2.2.quote: Under MP, each voter is constrained to one vote for each candidate:
C2.2.note: Under CV the input is an allocation of a budget of K (possibly fractional) votes over candidates; under MP one vote for each of the K party candidates; voters may also abstain. CARD was considered but the input is a vote allocation with a budget constraint, not a score or utility report.

C2.3.quote: Party leaders and voters share the same objective: to maximize the number
C2.3.note: Voters have utility u(k) = (k/K)V from their party winning k seats, a party affiliation, and a private voting cost.

C2.4.quote: each party member’s votes maximize the number of seats won by
C2.4.note: Votes (x_ip) and utilities u(k) / voting costs c_i have separate notation; votes and turnout are chosen to maximize the party's seats net of costs.

C3.1.quote: each voter decides whether or not to vote
C3.1.note: In every analysis voters choose turnout and (in theory) vote distribution strategically; in the experiment participants freely choose whether to vote (vote distribution fixed by design). Voters never vote for the other party, so 'differs from held attitude' here means abstention and strategic allocation of votes.

C4.1.note: C2.2 includes none of RANK, WEAK, APPR, DICH, PAIR (coded OTH), although utilities u(k) are used.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences or an equivalent is not used.

C5.1.loc: Section 2.1, p. 6; Section 3.3, p. 12; Section 5, p. 17
C5.1.quote: Under CV, the minority always achieves substantive representation
C5.1.note: Proposition 1, the equilibrium predictions and the experimental results evaluate rules by the number/share of seats won by the minority party (group representation).

C5.2.quote: We denote by z the number of seats won by party m
C5.2.note: Representation is measured by seats won by the minority party, defined by party affiliation (a held attribute of voters including abstainers), not by the submitted votes.

VOT.quote_behav: each voter decides whether or not to vote
VOT.quote_info: Realized costs are private information, but the distribution F (c) is common
VOT.note: Voters choose turnout (cost-threshold strategies) and, in theory, vote distribution to maximize expected seats; in the experiment, participants choose turnout only. Party sizes and cost distribution known; others' realized costs unknown. Without costs (Prop. 1) information is not stated separately.

CAN.loc_behav: Section 2 Base Model, p. 5; Section 4 The Experiment, p. 13
CAN.quote_behav: each party list maximizes the number of seats won by the party
CAN.quote_info: Realized costs are private information, but the distribution F (c) is common
CAN.note: Party leaders, who propose the party's list of candidates (proponents of alternatives; CAN chosen over OTH as listed first). Strategic in the theory (choose number of candidates to maximize expected seats); number of candidates fixed exogenously at the theoretical optimum in the experiment. Leaders choose before costs are realized and know only the common-knowledge cost distribution F; common knowledge is stated in words for all players, so EXPLICIT (listed first under the doubt rule).

C7.1.loc: Section 1 Introduction, p. 4; Section 4 The Experiment, p. 13
C7.1.quote: The number of candidates fielded by each party under CV was set
C7.1.note: In the experimental analysis, voters (VOT) choose turnout freely/strategically while party leaders (CAN) have the number of candidates fixed exogenously (NONSTRAT), consistent with both coders' MIXED coding of CAN.

C7.2.quote: Historically, CV’s coordination problem is deferred to the parties’ leadership
C7.2.note: Fixing the number of candidates is justified by historical practice (leaders solve coordination, equal spreading is an easy default) and by the paper's focus on turnout; footnotes add citations.

C8.1.loc: Section 2, p. 5; Section 2.1, p. 7; Section 3.2, p. 9; Appendix
C8.1.quote: We focus on a semi-symmetric perfect Bayesian equilibrium such that within
C8.1.note: Without costs: equilibria in weakly undominated strategies of a two-stage game, solved as a two-player constant-sum game where neither party has a profitable deviation (NE, with stage structure SPE). With costs: semi-symmetric perfect Bayesian equilibrium of a three-stage game with private costs (SPE and BNE).

C7.1.reason: In the experiment voters choose turnout freely while leaders' candidate numbers are fixed exogenously, so one present type is STRAT and another NONSTRAT in the same analysis.
